chunks: 979 - Ahmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥarīz, from Murāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

"The sajdah of gratitude is obligatory upon every Muslim. By it you complete your salat (prayer), please your Lord, and the angels marvel at you. When the servant performs salat (prayer) and then performs the sajdah of gratitude, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, opens the veil between the servant and the angels, and He says:

"O My angels, look at My servant: he has performed My obligation, fulfilled My covenant, then prostrated to Me in gratitude for what I have bestowed upon him. O My angels, what does he have with Me?" He said: Then the angels say, "Our Lord, Your mercy." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what does he have?" The angels say, "Our Lord, Your Paradise." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what?" The angels say, "Our Lord, sufficiency in his important affair." Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Then what?" He said: Nothing of good remains except that the angels mention it. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says, "O My angels, then what?" The angels say, "Our Lord, we have no knowledge."
He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says, "I give thanks to him just as he gave thanks to Me, and I turn toward him with My grace, and I show him My Face."

key_terms.جَنَّتُكَ: Your Paradise, named among the rewards for the grateful servant
key_terms.رَحْمَتُكَ: Your mercy, the first reward mentioned by the angels
key_terms.سَجْدَةُ الشُّكْرِ: the prostration of gratitude performed in thanks to Allah
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat (prayer), which this act completes
key_terms.كِفَايَةُ مُهِمِّهِ: sufficing his important need or concern
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: described here as obligatory and binding

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue and significance of sajdat al-shukr after salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents sajdat al-shukr as a great act of worship that completes salat (prayer) and draws divine pleasure. It describes the heavenly honor given to the grateful servant, culminating in Allah’s special grace and acceptance. The narration emphasizes gratitude as both a devotional act and a means of attaining divine mercy and nearness.
